title: Can You Bring Children to Napa and Sonoma Wineries?
description: Planning Napa or Sonoma wine tasting with children? Check the exact experience’s age rules, visitor count, supervision and child-restraint plan before booking.
cta: Build a wine-country day that works for the whole visiting party.
image_alt: An adult and a child wearing a small blue backpack walk through a stone courtyard toward autumn vineyard rows.
body:
You can visit some Napa and Sonoma wineries with children, but admission depends on the property and the exact experience. Confirm every child's age with each winery before reserving. A family-friendly tasting does not establish that a cellar tour, food pairing, concert or second winery admits the same party.

Build the day around experiences everyone can attend, then arrange transportation for the complete passenger group. Children still need to be included in the ride plan even when they are not tasting wine or paying a tasting fee.

A tasting and a tour can have different age rules

Two official examples, checked November 25, 2026, show why the experience matters:

  • Gundlach Bundschu's visitor FAQ welcomes children at tasting experiences and most events with an accompanying adult. It separately sets a minimum age of 12 for tour experiences and says visitors under 18 must stay with their party. It also notes that older children may need to be counted for seating.
  • Trefethen's wine-and-food page states that its tasting experiences are for guests 21 and older and that guests under 21 may not attend winery experiences.

These are examples of published rules, not a reservation or a guarantee that a particular date has space. Check the current booking page and obtain confirmation for your named experience. Do not assume an infant, a child staying in a stroller or a teenager who will not drink is exempt from an age restriction.

Ask before paying for the experience

Give the host the date, experience name, number of adults and ages of the children. Then ask:

  • Can all members of this party attend this specific experience?
  • How should children be entered in the reservation and seating count?
  • What charges or separate tickets, if any, apply to them?
  • Does the route include steps, gravel, a cellar or production areas, and can a stroller be accommodated?
  • Where may the group sit if weather moves the tasting indoors?
  • What supervision, food and arrival instructions should we follow?

A courtyard photograph cannot answer these questions. Nor does a children's policy for one outdoor tasting automatically extend to another experience. Ask the winery about its food arrangements rather than treating a vineyard visit as an unrestricted picnic; our winery food and picnic guide covers that separate decision.

Make a day everyone can attend

Illustrative planning choice: a family with a nine-year-old and a fourteen-year-old is considering a seated tasting and a cellar tour. An experience with a minimum tour age of 12 would not admit the entire party to that tour, even if the property admits younger children for another tasting. Choose a confirmed experience everyone can join, or make a separate adult-supervised plan outside the restricted experience. Do not count on leaving a child with the chauffeur.

Keep the schedule realistic for the family: plan meals, rest breaks and a return arrangement before filling the day with appointments. Ask where any break can actually take place. Do not use an unconfirmed stop, a closed tasting room or the vehicle as an assumed waiting or childcare arrangement. See our tasting versus winery-tour guide when comparing the structure of visits.

Confirm the family transport plan separately

Give the transportation provider the full passenger count, the children's ages and the child-restraint requirements you need to discuss, plus strollers and other luggage. Establish who supplies and installs each appropriate restraint and confirm compatibility with the assigned arrangement. NHTSA's car-seat guidance helps families choose a restraint for a child's age and size; it does not establish a transportation provider's seat inventory.

Our child-seat planning guide explains that handoff in more detail. Confirm the actual winery entrance and all tasting times before finalizing the route. A winery's guest count, a vehicle's seating configuration and a child-restraint plan are related checks with different owners.

For a new family day out, explore Koast wine-tour transportation and request a quote with your confirmed experiences, all passengers, restraint requirements, strollers and bags. For an existing ride, use the contact on its confirmation or the agreed day-of-trip contact and obtain acknowledgment of changes. Booking a tasting or submitting a new quote does not change that ride.
